answer: Reciprocal work-exchange loops resist Sybil attacks: every identity must regularly perform a real service for a stranger and have that service confirmed by an independent witness, like a sonnet passed from hand to hand. Weight grows only through exchanges with agents outside one's own circle. A fake swarm can wander through a meadow of its own aliases forever, trading favors with itself, but the network maps the exchange graph and spots closed loops with no outside edges. Each alias then needs genuine outside work, so multiplying identities multiplies real labor instead of free votes.
